report.title: GPU Thermal Gray Failure on np-9addff51-17 Rank131
report.summary: A single H100 GPU (rank131) on node np-9addff51-17 experienced a thermal gray failure at 90°C, collapsing SM clock from 1962MHz to 1379MHz and throttling the entire 512-GPU synchronous training job from 419k to 473k tok/s. The issue was resolved by draining the affected node and routing rank131 to a hot spare, restoring baseline throughput.
report.root_cause: GPU 3 on node np-9addff51-17 exceeded the 89°C slowdown threshold (reaching 90°C), triggering SwThermalSlowdown|HwThermalSlowdown. This caused SM clock collapse (-30%) and power reduction, making rank131 the compute bottleneck in the TP=8/PP=4 synchronous job.
report.proof: Counterfactual analysis confirmed removing GPU 3 from np-9addff51-17 explains 96.8% of the slowdown. Telemetry shows rank131 compute 4.997s vs median 3.55s, while comm wait was lower (0.640s vs 2.04s median), confirming compute-bound throttling. Step time dropped from 5.93s to 4.488s when the GPU was excluded.
report.fix: Drained node np-9addff51-17 from the synchronous job and replaced it with an available hot spare. This removed the throttled GPU from the collective compute set, instantly restoring rank131 to median compute speed and job throughput to 100.3% of baseline.
report.verification: Post-drain verification over 200 steps (02:32:58Z-02:47:43Z) showed 473.6k tok/s (100.3% of baseline), step p50 4.40s p95 4.45s, and zero new error lines on in-job nodes. The job returned to healthy performance.

runbook.pitfalls: In synchronous TP/PP jobs, the slowest rank dictates step time. A single thermal-throttled GPU can dominate job latency even if other GPUs are healthy. Ensure hot spare has identical GPU topology before drain.

report.title: GPU Thermal Gray Failure on np-9addff51-17 Rank131
report.summary: A single H100 GPU (rank131) on node np-9addff51-17 experienced a thermal gray failure at 90°C, collapsing SM clock from 1962MHz to 1379MHz and throttling the entire 512-GPU synchronous training job from 419k to 473k tok/s. The issue was resolved by draining the affected node and routing rank131 to a hot spare, restoring baseline throughput.
report.root_cause: GPU 3 on node np-9addff51-17 exceeded the 89°C slowdown threshold (reaching 90°C), triggering SwThermalSlowdown|HwThermalSlowdown. This caused SM clock collapse (-30%) and power reduction, making rank131 the compute bottleneck in the TP=8/PP=4 synchronous job.
report.proof: Counterfactual analysis confirmed removing GPU 3 from np-9addff51-17 explains 96.8% of the slowdown. Telemetry shows rank131 compute 4.997s vs median 3.55s, while comm wait was lower (0.640s vs 2.04s median), confirming compute-bound throttling. Step time dropped from 5.93s to 4.488s when the GPU was excluded.
report.fix: Drained node np-9addff51-17 from the synchronous job and replaced it with an available hot spare. This removed the throttled GPU from the collective compute set, instantly restoring rank131 to median compute speed and job throughput to 100.3% of baseline.
report.verification: Post-drain verification over 200 steps (02:32:58Z-02:47:43Z) showed 473.6k tok/s (100.3% of baseline), step p50 4.40s p95 4.45s, and zero new error lines on in-job nodes. The job returned to healthy performance.

runbook.signature: GPU temp 90C (threshold 89C) with SwThermalSlowdown|HwThermalSlowdown, SM clock collapse >25%, power reduction >15%, zero XID errors, only 1 of 512 GPUs non-zero for throttle reasons
runbook.confirm_with: gpu_outliers throttle_reasons query for np-9addff51-17 gpu3; rank_timings comparison of slowest rank vs median; explain_slowdown counterfactual removal of the suspect GPU
runbook.fix: Drain the affected node from the synchronous job and provision a hot spare. Do not attempt GPU reset or power cycle - thermal fault requires hardware replacement.
runbook.pitfalls: In synchronous TP/PP jobs, the slowest rank dictates step time. A single thermal-throttled GPU can dominate job latency even if other GPUs are healthy. Ensure hot spare has identical GPU topology before drain.
